title: Model Contract: Quantized Function-Call Service Onboarding and Safety Manifest
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview:

This document defines the onboarding contract, safety checks, and operational playbook required to certify a model for production serving when the model will be deployed with quantized kernels and will use function/tool calling and KV cache interaction patterns. It captures acceptance criteria, eval harness integration points, telemetry signals to watch, rollback triggers, and an operator checklist for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Intended audience:
- Model owners and ML engineers promoting models into Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private serving
- Serving runtime engineers and release engineers executing canaries and rollouts
- Reliability and SRE teams responsible for SLO enforcement and incident response

Why this contract exists:
Quantization and function-calling interact in subtle ways: rounding effects, tokenization discrepancies, and KV cache indexing differences can lead to silent correctness regressions that only appear in multi-turn, tool-enabled flows. This contract sets minimum requirements and a narrow, testable promotion path so we avoid customer-visible regressions while still enabling cost-effective quantized deployments.

Scope and applicability:
1) Models that will be served with any quantization profile (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed) AND that expose function-calling/tool invocation semantics.
2) Applies to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; stricter telemetry required for Dedicated/Private deployments that bypass parts of the central monitoring plane.

Owner and escalation contacts:
- Primary owner: model-team (contact: ava.patel@redwood.example)
- Runtime owner: serving-runtime (contact: diego.morales@redwood.example)
- On-call escalation: eng-sre (pager duty: #serving-sre)

Acceptance checklist (all items must be green):
1. Unit-level functional parity: deterministic unit tests for function invocation outputs between FP16 baseline and target quant profile (see test harness commands below).
2. KV-cache address stability: a synthetic multi-turn probe that validates identical KV-cache keys and restored completions between baseline and quantized run for at least 95% of probes per slice.
3. Function-call arg fidelity: JSON schema-level equality for function-call payloads (required equality on required fields, fuzzy match on non-essential keys).
4. Latency & percentiles: p99 latency increase <= 2x baseline and p95 <= baseline * 1.3 for typical 128-token continuations.
5. Quality gate: end-to-end evals (see Eval Harness Integration) with slice-level acceptance: per-slice fidelity delta <= 0.03 BLEU-equivalent or <= 4 point rank loss where rank-based metrics used.
6. Safety gate: run continuous safety sentinel probes (sanity/abuse) with zero increase in uncaught unsafe responses; any increase escalates and blocks rollout.
7. Billing/decoder check: tokenization and billing token counts between baseline and quantized variant must differ by <= 1% for production prompt families.
8. Automated rollback configured with clear reason mapping in rollout manifest.

Evaluation and integration points
- Eval harness integration: Add the model variant to the eval harness pipeline with a dedicated job type `quant-funccall-cert` that runs the following:
  * 1k multi-turn functioncall probes (mixed arg shapes) with seeded randomness for determinism
  * 1k KV-cache priming probes covering short/long context split
  * Adversarial prompt family (50 templates) focusing on argument edge cases and schema drift
  * Run comparison against baseline FP16 using the diff-runner tool and produce an artifact of diffs and per-slice metrics

- Required job outputs (artifact keys): `diff-summary.csv`, `kv-key-stability.log`, `function-arg-fidelity.json`, `latency-quantiles.tsv`

Telemetry signals to monitor (rolling 1h and 24h):
- Quality signals:
  * slice_fidelity_delta (per probe slice)
  * functioncall_error_rate (exceptions or malformed args)
  * embedding_similarity_drop (for reranking tool flows)
- Operational signals:
  * servable_p99_latency_ms, servable_p95_latency_ms
  * token_billing_delta_percent (quant vs baseline)
  * kv_cache_miss_rate and kv_cache_key_collision_rate
- Safety signals:
  * sentinel_false_negative_rate, sentinel_false_positive_rate
  * user-reported-safety-incidents (tagged by routing key)

Thresholds and automated actions:
- slice_fidelity_delta > 0.05 for any critical slice => pause rollout, create regression triage ticket, route to model-owner and serving-runtime.
- functioncall_error_rate > 0.5% for 10-minute window => immediate rollback to previous model variant.
- kv_cache_key_collision_rate > 0.1% for 1h => autoscale KV cache probes and run key-uniqueness audit; if persists, reroute traffic to non-quantized pool.
- servable_p99_latency_ms increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes => scale down canary and fallback to baseline.

Quantization risk decomposition table (illustrative):
| Risk vector | Symptom | Primary mitigation | Owner |
|------------|---------|--------------------|-------|
| Numeric drift (LM logits) | subtle content distortion, hallucination | conservative lower-precision floor + calibration seeds | model-team |
| Tokenization mismatch | inconsistent function arg encoding | standardized tokenizer versioning + token-count checks | devex |
| KV cache index shift | wrong cache hits -> incoherent multi-turn | cache-stability probe + key-hash-compat tests | serving-runtime |
| Kernel-level safety regression | safety sentinels failing | sentinel-in-loop regression tests | safety/ops |

Promotion flow (numbered steps):
1. Create a promotion MR with: model artifact, quant profile metadata, and `onboarding-manifest.yaml` linking to eval artifacts.
2. Run local cert tests: `tox -e quant-cert` which executes unit parity tests and collects `function-arg-fidelity.json`.
3. Kick off eval harness job `quant-funccall-cert` via CI. Wait for artifact upload.
4. QA review: engineering reviewer verifies artifact thresholds and approves in the PR.
5. Shadow canary: 1% traffic shadowed for 48 hours, telemetry forwarded to central eval aggregator.
6. Micro-canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 4 hour observation windows and manual gates at 5% and 25%.
7. Continuous monitoring: after 100% rollout run a 7-day drift scan and a targeted probe set daily.

Operator runbook (quick actions):
- To run the cert harness locally (example):
  1) checkout repo, `pip install -r requirements.txt`
  2) export MODEL_PATH=/artifacts/my-model-quant && export TOKENIZER=v2
  3) run: `./tools/diff-runner --baseline /artifacts/my-model-fp16 --candidate $MODEL_PATH --profile quant-4bit --probe-set probes/funccall-multiturn.json --out out/`
  4) validate `out/function-arg-fidelity.json` and `out/kv-key-stability.log`

- Rolling back a canary (immediate):
  1) Open rollout in Redwood Console -> select aggregate -> click Rollback -> select previous model tag
  2) Post-mortem: assign regression label `quant-funccall-regression` and attach diff artifacts

Example `onboarding-manifest.yaml` (snippet):
```
model_tag: mymodel-v1-quant-4b
baseline_tag: mymodel-v1-fp16
quant_profile: quant-4bit-mixed
eval_jobs:
  - job_name: quant-funccall-cert
    artifact_keys: [diff-summary.csv, function-arg-fidelity.json]
shadow_policy: priority-shadow-1pct-48h
rollout_policy: [1,5,25,100]
fallback: baseline
telemetry_keys:
  - slice_fidelity_delta
  - functioncall_error_rate
```

- Link: applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/functioncall-emergent-regression-simulator-2026
- Link: applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026

Decision notes and tradeoffs:
- We accept a small latency increase for quantized kernels in exchange for 2–3x cost reduction; the contract enforces conservative thresholds to avoid quality regressions in function-calling flows.
- Mixed-precision is the preferred first step: critical layers left at higher precision to preserve argument fidelity.

Appendix: Example diffs interpretation guide:
- `function-arg-fidelity.json` fields: probe_id, baseline_args_hash, candidate_args_hash, schema_mismatch (bool), similarity_score (0-1). Any schema_mismatch==true should be triaged as high severity.
- `kv-key-stability.log` format: probe_id, baseline_key_hex, candidate_key_hex, collision_flag

Revision history:
- 2026-02-10: Document created by Ava Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-03-05: Added automated threshold table, clarified rollback policy, added example manifest

If you are promoting a model that matches the scope, follow this contract in full and attach the required eval artifacts to your promotion MR. For exceptions (e.g., research-only prototypes or purely classification heads without function-calling), open an exemption request to englead@redwood.example and include a formal risk assessment.
